messages.subject: which sd values are correct when using 'summary.linear.predictor' versus 'summary.fitted.values' and a gamma distribution?
parts:
Hi, I'm trying to generate prediction maps by predicting at unsampled locations using an inla stack with covariates. The models are spatio-temporal and I've used a gamma distribution and the dependent variable is tree density (I've added 0.00001 to the values so that density values of zero does not cause a problem). After setting up a prediction stack, I've used both the 'summary.linear.predictor' and the 'summary.fitted.values' to extract the predicted values. While the predicted mean values are similar after back transforming  the 'summary.linear.predictor', the sd values are not. I would like to generate prediction maps of both the mean and the sd (to highlight where there is greater prediction uncertainty). But which of the two sd values should I trust? I understand that the sd would be different because the un-transformed mean values are different..Also, does it make sense to minus the adjusted value ( 0.00001) from the sd as well (even if this is done, they are still different). 


#-- Call INLA and get results --#
mod =   inla(formula,
             data=inla.stack.data(stfull),
             family="gamma",control.family = list(link = "log"),
             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stfull), link=1,compute=TRUE,quantiles=NULL),inla.setOption(scale.model.default = TRUE),
             control.results=list(return.marginals.random=FALSE,
return.marginals.predictor=FALSE), verbose=TRUE)

print(summary(mod))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] which sd values are correct when using 'summary.linear.predictor' versus 'summary.fitted.values' and a gamma distribution?
parts:
Hi,
The standard deviation of a transformation is _not_ the transformation of the standard deviation, so exp(sd) in your code is incorrect.
Quantiles transform like that, but not moments.
If your posteriors are skewed, use quantiles instead of moments when possible.
The moments of fitted.values are the moments of the transformed distribution, so those are the ones you should use if you need them.

Finn

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] which sd values are correct when using 'summary.linear.predictor' versus 'summary.fitted.values' and a gamma distribution?
parts:
Hi,

For practical convenience, I almost always use quantiles (including median instead of mean). Because I do not know what is the "right parametrisation", x, or exp(x), sigma or variance. With quantiles, you can transform them back and forth at will.

You can usually report "median" ("0.025 quantile", "0.975 quantile") when you do applications, e.g: 7 (5.4, 20)

For spatial plots you then need 2 quantile-plots instead of 1 sd-plot, so here it is more debatable what to do. But the sd plot on fitted.value-scale may not represent what you think it represents! The "uncertainty" on this scale is often not "symmetric", making sd a less useful summary statistic (quantiles are still good).

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] which sd values are correct when using 'summary.linear.predictor' versus 'summary.fitted.values' and a gamma distribution?
parts:
Here are my 2 cents.

I tend to display 4 maps. 
1) the mean or median to display the estimates itself.
2) the 2.5% percentile. High values on this map indicate areas where you are pretty sure that the phenomenon is present.
3) the 97.5 percentile. Low values on this map indicate areas where you are pretty sure that the phenomenon is absent.
4) the difference (identity link) or ratio (log link) between the 97.5% percentile and 2.5% percentile. This displays the uncertainty.

Best regards,
